en: No matter if you are working with a general
agent, a task-specific agent, or if you're
building one, one of the most important
things both you as the developer of an agent
as well as the user of an agent must do is
managing its context window. And with that,
I don't mean that you have to prevent it
from overflowing. Sure, you should try to
start new sessions whenever you're about to
tackle a new complex task to avoid that.
But what I mean is that you must make sure
that you do provide all the relevant context
for a task you want the agent to tackle.
Now, that of course includes the team, the
company that built the agent.
They do, for example, provide the tools.
They do
provide a system instruction, which is a
hidden instruction that's baked into the
agent that, for example, controls its tone
or anything like that. And you
also have some control because there are
some core
building blocks you should be aware of when
building an agent or when working with an
agent. And it comes down to a term called
context engineering, which is all about
making sure
that your agent, and therefore in the end,
the large language model, the brain that's
powering the agent, which is one core
building block, of course, has all the
relevant context it needs to complete a
task.
Now, these building blocks of an agent would
of course be the model as a brain. It would
be the tools, and that is something you
typically don't specify as the user of an
agent, but as the person who builds it, you
do, or as the team who builds it. You define
which tools are exposed by the agent to the
model in the end, so by the harness to the
model.
You as the builder of an agent also define
some of the instructions, those hidden
system instructions, for example, but as the
user of an agent,
you also have some influence there. You can
also set up some general instructions, some
project-specific instructions, and we'll
dive into that in the next section.
And then there are some other relevant
building blocks as well, which also control
what an agent can see,
what it can do. And again, we'll dive into
that in the next section. And then later,
once we start into building agents, you'll
also see many of these building blocks
again.
